label: Inert emptiness from three grounding principles
description: New non-transcription conditional support option for premise A2 (inert emptiness) of Arrival A, composed from nothingFromNothing and inertOfNothingFromNothing. In a history with a concrete-empty moment s and a concrete thing x present at a later t, x has not been present at s, so it began and has a concrete ground; that ground has not wholly ceased before s; following grounds down a well-founded chain of present concrete things ends at a concrete thing present at s, contradicting emptiness. All three premises are OPEN framework inputs about every history of the model; each is needed (controls 1 to 3), and together they do not contain the possibility of a necessary concrete being (control 4). In Arrival A, necessity still comes from the possible contingent-free past, presence-to-existence and the frame premises. The three premises are not shown to be better warranted than A2; they make its warrant explicit as a causal principle for beginnings, a no-gap condition on grounds and well-founded grounding. Nothing is attributed to a source. No premise truth is established.
